You may edit ONLY: storygame/story_package/authoring_view.py, tests/test_authoring_view.py, tests/shard_durations.json (the first two are new files).

BACKGROUND. Frontend judging tools (frontend/e2e/authored-spans.js, knowledge-available.js, roleplay-judge.test.js and the tools that import them) read the story through five flat legacy files (knowledge.yaml, handoffs.yaml, pacing.yaml, storylet-routes.yaml, plot.md) that no longer exist in data/stories/continuity-initiative/; the default story is now the compiled tree under source/ and is loaded by `storygame.story_package.loader.load_story_package(Path(root))` into a pydantic `StoryPackage`. The old files survive only as a FROZEN parity fixture in tests/fixtures/parity/continuity-initiative/legacy/ (use it to learn the SHAPES; its text is out of date, never read it at runtime). Task: build a Python exporter that projects the LIVE package into those legacy shapes, so the JavaScript can be repointed in the next round without changing its consumers or its inline test fixtures.

BUILD `storygame/story_package/authoring_view.py` (shared code: story-agnostic, no story, scene or character names):
  def authoring_view(package: StoryPackage) -> dict[str, object]  # JSON-serialisable, deterministic
returning exactly these top-level keys, each in the legacy file's shape:
  'knowledge'  : same shape as legacy knowledge.yaml (`package.knowledge.model_dump(mode='json')` already has the same top-level keys: facts, knowledge, scene_frames, schema_version).
  'pacing'     : same shape as legacy pacing.yaml (`package.pacing.model_dump(mode='json')`: budget_seconds, ending, events, scenes, transitions).
  'handoffs'   : {'deliveries': [...]} with the legacy delivery records (fact_id, cue_text, fallback_text and whatever other keys the legacy records carry that the JS reads) projected from `package.deliveries`.
  'routes'     : legacy storylet-routes.yaml shape for the keys the JS reads: 'canonical_bridge_events' and 'canonical_resolution_events' (the compiled package names them bridge_events and resolution_events), each event with its id, fallback_text and produces list (items with fact_id) plus the other keys the JS reads, and 'storylets'. Read the frontend files to learn exactly which keys are read: grep for routePackage, routes., knowledgePackage, handoffs., pacing., frame. in frontend/e2e/*.js (read only).
  'frames'     : the plot.md scene frames the JS reads, as {scene_id: {'scene_id', 'entry_text', 'entry_variants': [{'text', ...}], 'bridge_text': {transition_id: text}}} built from each loaded scene's metadata (entry_text, entry_variants, bridge_text).
Also add a module CLI: `python -m storygame.story_package.authoring_view STORY_ROOT [--out PATH]` that loads the package from STORY_ROOT and prints the JSON (or writes it to PATH), exit 0; non-existent root exits non-zero with a one-line message.

TESTS (tests/test_authoring_view.py, hermetic, no network, fast): (1) against the default story root `data/stories/continuity-initiative`: top-level keys exactly the five above; knowledge top-level keys equal the frozen fixture's; every knowledge item with a delivery_text keeps it; routes has both canonical lists non-empty and each event has an id; frames has an entry_text for every scene that has one in the loaded package, equal to the scene metadata value; handoffs deliveries non-empty with fact_id; (2) shape check against the frozen fixture: for each of knowledge claim items, pacing events/transitions and route events, the set of keys the exporter emits is a superset of the keys the JavaScript reads (list those keys in the test as constants with a comment naming the JS file that reads them); (3) the result round-trips through json.dumps/json.loads and two calls return equal dicts; (4) the CLI via subprocess prints valid JSON for the default root and fails on a missing root. Register the new test file: run `.venv/bin/python scripts/regen_shard_durations.py --missing-only` and keep only the one new entry.

Do NOT edit any JavaScript, any story data, or any existing test. Say in NOTES.txt which keys you found the JS reading and any compiled-versus-legacy difference you could not project.
